neighbours.label: Pacific island place names in the middle of a name (Micronesia, Polynesia, Caroline Islands) in plant/history context
fire: Botanists think the breadfruit was carried by canoe across Polynesia long before European contact.
Archaeologists dated the pottery on Yap, in the Caroline Islands of Micronesia, to roughly two thousand years ago.
Early voyagers noted that taro was cultivated on every high island of the South Pacific.
Linguists trace the Austronesian languages through Melanesia and into Polynesia.
The wartime airfield on Guam sits in the Mariana chain of western Micronesia.
Missionaries introduced new crops to Tahiti and the Society Islands in the early nineteenth century.
Sailors stopped at Tonga and Samoa to take on yams before crossing Polynesia again.
The kava plant is grown across Vanuatu and much of Melanesia.
quiet: Botanists think the potato was carried by traders across the Andes long before European contact.
Archaeologists dated the pottery found in Cyprus to roughly two thousand years ago.
Early travelers noted that wheat was cultivated on every plateau of the Anatolian interior.
Linguists trace the Bantu languages through Cameroon and into the Congo basin.
The wartime airfield outside Norwich sits in the flat farmland of eastern England.
Missionaries introduced new crops to Peru and the Andean highlands in the early nineteenth century.
Sailors stopped at Malta and Crete to take on olives before crossing the Mediterranean again.
The saffron crocus is grown across Kashmir and much of Iran.

notes: Model pilot (sonnet arm; the same pole is tested independently by the other arm, pairing disclosed): this pole reads the held pole bonsai1/L12/N4075+ (zeroing the anchor removes 1.00 of this pole's activation), from a batched edge measurement with 8 same-layer placebos. Label and all 16 sentences written by the Sonnet 5.5 labeller from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + the edge hint) and one probe round of 8 sentences (none reused). An Opus gate checked rule-level items only and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Only the Micronesia probe cleared 0.3 (0.42); Fiji, Mauritius and the Caribbean stayed under 0.1. So the label sticks to Pacific names mid-name in botanical/historical prose, with other regions as near misses.
